requirement: A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
rationale:
**Judgment: `requirements.ci.span` is satisfied.** The implementation covers every obligation, the {impl} markers are complete, and the tests exercise the main boundaries and failure cases.

**Implementation**
- **Fence recognition.** `colon_fence` in `src/lib.rs` accepts at least three colons, allows up to three leading spaces, and rejects four or more (and tabs).
- **Opening fence.** `definition_blocks` in `src/lib.rs` requires `{req}` immediately after the colons and then whitespace and a valid name. `:::{req}ready` is therefore not an opener, and an opener indented four or more spaces is not an opener either. An opener inside a Markdown code block is ignored through `overlaps_protected`.
- **Closing fence.** The block ends at the first later line that is not inside a code block, is a colon fence with `count >= fence_length`, and has only whitespace after the colons. Lines such as `:::foo` and four-space-indented `:::` do not close the block. If no closer is found, the block is marked `closed = false`.
- **Body.** It runs from `body_start` (just after the opening line) to `body_end` (the start of the closing line). That keeps headings, setext headings, code fences containing `:::`, nested shorter directives and blank lines. Nothing after the closing fence is included, because `end` stops at the end of the closing line.
- **Comparison text.** `collect_definitions` in `src/evidence.rs` builds the text with `without_options(...).trim()`, so leading and trailing whitespace is excluded. Removing option lines is specified by `requirements.references.anchors`, which those functions also mark as implemented.
- **Missing closer.** `collect_definitions` reports a missing closing fence as an error.
- **Fenced references.** `opening_fence` and `closes` in `src/fenced.rs` reuse the same fence rules for `{impl}`/`{cite}`/`{test}` fences and are marked {impl}.
- **Marking.** I found no unmarked code that parses requirement spans. `marker_ranges` in `src/index.rs` and `replace_definitions` in `src/lib.rs` only consume `definition_blocks` results or reuse `colon_fence`.

**Tests**
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers a body containing a code fence with `:::`, an ATX heading, a setext heading and blank lines. It also checks that text after the closer is excluded and that a second requirement follows correctly.
- `requirement_bodies_are_compared_without_surrounding_whitespace` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers whitespace trimming.
- `validates_full_names_requirement_text_and_input_lines` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers a body containing a fenced example.
- `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers the unclosed case and the error text.
- `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` (`src/lib.rs`) covers a longer fence containing a nested shorter directive.
- `closing_fences_allow_no_trailing_text_and_fences_allow_three_spaces_of_indent` (`src/lib.rs`) covers:
  - `:::foo` not closing the block;
  - `::: ` with trailing whitespace closing it;
  - three-space indentation being accepted;
  - four-space indentation being rejected as an opener and as a closer;
  - `:::{req}ready` not being an opener.

I found no acknowledged gaps (no FIXMEs) and no unacknowledged gaps.
